name: Fidelity

profile.address: 11050, Cornhusker Road, Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68218
profile.reading:
Fidelity Investments, the Boston-headquartered, privately held mutual fund and brokerage giant, built this data center in Papillion, Nebraska, a suburb of Omaha in Sarpy County, as part of a broader push by financial-services firms in the early 2010s to build out disaster-resilient, lower-cost computing infrastructure in the country's interior. The project was first disclosed publicly in October 2012 under the internal code name "Project Photon," before Fidelity's name was confirmed as the company behind it. Trade press coverage at the time put the investment at roughly $200 million, with construction beginning immediately and the facility targeted to be operational by 2014. Fidelity said the site would employ around 30 to 35 people once running, and confirmed it was designed to meet LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) green-building standards.

Nebraska's incentive package was a significant part of the story: Fidelity became the first company to make use of the state's "Tier 2 Plus-Large Data Center" provision, a category added to the Nebraska Advantage Act during the 2012 legislative session specifically to attract large-scale data center investment. Then-Governor Dave Heineman held the project up publicly as a model for other companies weighing Nebraska as a data center location, part of a run of financial- and technology-sector announcements that helped establish the greater Omaha-Papillion corridor as a genuine, if lower-profile, U.S. data center market built around relatively cheap power, lower natural-disaster exposure than many coastal markets, and favorable state tax treatment. Local infrastructure records from the period also note that water and sewer line extensions tied to the project were expected to accelerate development in the western part of Papillion's jurisdiction.

Consistent with Fidelity's other data center investments around the country, the Papillion facility supports the company's own internal financial-services technology, trading systems, account management, and other mutual-fund and brokerage operations, rather than operating as a commercial colocation facility open to outside tenants. Because Fidelity is a privately held, employee- and family-controlled company rather than a publicly traded one, it does not file the SEC disclosures that might otherwise surface facility-level operating detail, and it has not published updated capacity, square footage, or expansion figures for this site since the original 2012 announcement. What is known publicly about this building rests almost entirely on that initial wave of local and trade-press coverage from 2012 rather than on any ongoing disclosure from Fidelity itself, which is typical for a large financial institution that treats its own back-office infrastructure as an operational detail rather than a marketing point.

reading:
Fidelity Investments is the privately held Boston asset manager and brokerage, held through its parent FMR LLC, and the single facility attached to this record is its data centre at Papillion, Nebraska, in Sarpy County southwest of Omaha. Fidelity built and runs the site for its own account. It is not colocation, and no part of it is marketed to outside tenants.

The project was announced in October 2012 after being carried under the code name Project Photon, with a stated investment of about 200 million dollars, construction starting immediately, an operational target of 2014, a design intended to reach LEED certification, and an expected permanent staff of 30 to 35. That widely repeated 200 million dollar figure is the announcement number, and the state's own incentive record shows it understates what Fidelity ultimately committed. The Nebraska Department of Revenue publishes the complete list of applications filed under the Nebraska Advantage Act between 2006 and 2020, and that list records two separate applications by FMR LLC at Papillion. One is entered at 390 in the investment column, which the table states is in millions of dollars, against a commitment of 30 full time equivalent jobs. The other is entered at 150 million dollars with no job commitment. Together they describe roughly 540 million dollars of committed investment rather than 200 million. Fidelity was the first user of the state's large data centre tier, a category added to the Act in the 2012 legislative session specifically to attract projects of this size, and the Act stopped accepting new applications after 31 December 2020.

What Nebraska's incentive record does not do is establish capacity. The department's table reports dollars and jobs, not power. Fidelity has published no IT load, no utility service figure, no standby generator count and no floor area for Papillion, and because FMR LLC is privately held it files no annual report on Form 10-K in which a properties section would list the site. Everything technical about this campus is therefore unestablished, and any megawatt number circulating for it does not come from Fidelity or from the State of Nebraska.

The registry row itself derives from OpenStreetMap way 421273622, an outline first drawn in 2016 with no name and no operator. The Fidelity operator tag and the telecom=data_center tag were added together on 30 April 2023 in changeset 135521451, a 95 change edit whose comment reads "Omaha cleaninging up notes" and which closed five user submitted map notes in the Omaha area. That is an ordinary and defensible origin for the tag rather than a suspect one, and the underlying facility is real and well documented in the public record of Nebraska's incentive programme. It is the capacity, not the existence, that is missing.
